## Technical Overview

This page is a self-contained webR-powered Shiny application. It runs R entirely in your browser using WebAssembly. This approach eliminates the need for a traditional R server (like Shiny Server or Posit Connect), making it highly portable and scalable.

### How it Works
1. **WebAssembly (Wasm)**: R is compiled to Wasm via the [webR](https://docs.r-wasm.org/webr/latest/) project.
2. **Service Workers**: The application uses a Service Worker to manage the webR lifecycle and cache assets.
3. **Shinylive**: This Quarto extension bundles the Shiny UI and server logic into the static page.

## Performance Tester

The following Shiny application will automatically run several benchmarks to evaluate the performance of R on your current machine and browser.

```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 800

library(shiny)
library(bslib)

ui <- page_fluid(
  theme = bs_theme(version = 5, bootswatch = "cosmo"),
  titlePanel("webR Performance Diagnostics"),

  layout_column_wrap(
    width = 1/2,
    card(
      card_header("System Information"),
      tableOutput("sys_info")
    ),
    card(
      card_header("Performance Metrics"),
      tableOutput("perf_metrics"),
      downloadButton("download_results", "Download Results (CSV)", class = "btn-primary mt-3")
    )
  ),

  card(
    card_header("Execution Lag Test"),
    p("This test measures the round-trip time for a simple R command execution."),
    plotOutput("lag_plot", height = "300px"),
    actionButton("run_lag_test", "Re-run Lag Test", class = "btn-secondary mt-2")
  ),

  card(
    card_header("Technical Details for Developers"),
    accordion(
      accordion_panel(
        "Load Process",
        p("1. The browser downloads the webR Wasm binary (~25MB compressed)."),
        p("2. The webR worker is initialized."),
        p("3. The Shiny application code is sent to the worker."),
        p("4. R packages are loaded from the R-Wasm repo if needed.")
      ),
      accordion_panel(
        "Benchmarking Methodology",
        p("Total Load Time: Measured using `performance.now()` from the earliest possible moment in the HTML head until the Shiny server session is initialized and sends a request back to JS."),
        p("Lag: Calculated by recording the time before and after a series of simple R operations to gauge the responsiveness of the webR worker.")
      )
    )
  ),

  # JS to get browser info and timing
  tags$script("
    Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler('get_browser_info', function(message) {
      const info = {
        userAgent: navigator.userAgent,
        hardwareConcurrency: navigator.hardwareConcurrency || 'unknown',
        totalLoadTime: performance.now() - (window.pageLoadStartTime || 0)
      };
      Shiny.setInputValue('browser_info_response', info);
    });
  ")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  # Reactive values to store performance data
  perf_data <- reactiveValues(
    lag_samples = numeric(),
    browser_info = list(userAgent = "Loading...", hardwareConcurrency = "unknown", totalLoadTime = NULL)
  )

  # Capture browser info via JS
  observe({
    session$sendCustomMessage("get_browser_info", list())
  })

  observeEvent(input$browser_info_response, {
    perf_data$browser_info <- input$browser_info_response
  })

  # Lag testing function
  run_lag_test <- function() {
    samples <- 20
    times <- numeric(samples)
    for (i in 1:samples) {
      start <- Sys.time()
      # Simple operation
      invisible(1 + 1)
      times[i] <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), start, units = "secs")) * 1000
    }
    perf_data$lag_samples <- times
  }

  # Auto-run lag test on load
  observe({
    run_lag_test()
  }, suspended = FALSE)

  observeEvent(input$run_lag_test, {
    run_lag_test()
  })

  output$sys_info <- renderTable({
    data.frame(
      Property = c("R Version", "Platform", "Browser Agent", "Hardware Concurrency"),
      Value = c(
        R.version.string,
        R.version$platform,
        perf_data$browser_info$userAgent,
        as.character(perf_data$browser_info$hardwareConcurrency)
      )
    )
  })

  output$perf_metrics <- renderTable({
    avg_lag <- if(length(perf_data$lag_samples) > 0) mean(perf_data$lag_samples) else NA
    total_load <- if(!is.null(perf_data$browser_info$totalLoadTime)) perf_data$browser_info$totalLoadTime / 1000 else NA

    data.frame(
      Metric = c("Total Load Time (JS Start -> R Ready)", "Average Execution Lag", "Min Lag", "Max Lag"),
      Value = c(
        paste0(round(total_load, 2), " seconds"),
        paste0(round(avg_lag, 2), " ms"),
        paste0(round(min(perf_data$lag_samples), 2), " ms"),
        paste0(round(max(perf_data$lag_samples), 2), " ms")
      )
    )
  })

  output$lag_plot <- renderPlot({
    req(length(perf_data$lag_samples) > 0)
    plot(perf_data$lag_samples, type = "b", pch = 19, col = "#007bff",
         xlab = "Sample Number", ylab = "Lag (ms)",
         main = "Internal R Execution Latency Samples")
    grid()
  })

  output$download_results <- downloadHandler(
    filename = function() {
      paste("webr-benchmarks-", Sys.Date(), ".csv", sep = "")
    },
    content = function(file) {
      df <- data.frame(
        timestamp = Sys.time(),
        total_load_time_sec = if(!is.null(perf_data$browser_info$totalLoadTime)) perf_data$browser_info$totalLoadTime / 1000 else NA,
        avg_lag_ms = mean(perf_data$lag_samples),
        user_agent = perf_data$browser_info$userAgent,
        cores = perf_data$browser_info$hardwareConcurrency,
        r_version = R.version.string,
        platform = R.version$platform
      )
      write.csv(df, file, row.names = FALSE)
    }
  )
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```
